questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an English speaking country. England has a nice culture and Newcastle seemed like a cool city. I didn't want to go to a school where the workload was bigger than in UCPH.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It wasn't the time of my life but it has been cool and I met some fun people.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Really easy. Newcastle uni has a huge welcome program and they help you all the way. You just have to check your mails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a free ride in a taxi from the airport to my accommodation which was arranged by the uni.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They appoint a peer mentor and a tutor (a teacher that helps you) and you can ask them any questions you have.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was really easy to get into Leazes Parade. I saw someone else's travel report, which said not to go there because of mold, but because it was so easy I tried my luck anyway. And I have been really happy staying here. It's for european students only. I did not experience mold and I have to say that if you experience mold then it is probably your own fault for not using the heater enough and not opening the windows. The people I live with have not had any problems with it, and any issues that have arisen have been fixed quickly.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Leazes Parade is a bit far fra campus and so is grocery stores, so you do a lot of walking.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You wish for courses and you don't know if you get them until after your arrival. I don't remember the specifics, but I remember I found it quite easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
You can ask your tutor and mentor. They also make sure your courses don't overlap. You can also change courses in the first 2 weeks of classes. I didn't do it but it's good to know.
It was quite hard to navigate in the timetables. I gave up, but it might be worth it to plan better than I did, to have less days in school.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got what I wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry about the courses before you arrive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Probably a bit lower than in UCPH, but because they are in English, they seem pretty equal.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Quite informal and definitely more informal than I expected. They take attendance, which is a bit annoying, but they usually film classes so you can rewatch them while studying (or if you were sick).
a lot more lectures and less seminars than in DK.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Legal institutions and methods LAW1210 - BA class - a lot of reading - quite easy - exam is 8 hour take home - the 1st years from England were kind of confused so the seminars were a bit annoying to attend, because the level was dumbed down a bit for them...
Law and literature LAW3029 - Not a lot of law focus - if you like English literature then it's pretty interesting - The lectures were pretty much just the teacher talking - essay exam.
Energy Justice LAW8583 - also not too much law focus - good teacher - the lectures had more engagement and discussions - small class - essay exam

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the two latter courses if the topics interest you. I had the first class recommended, but I don't think it was very fun and it definitely was not necessary for my other classes to have an introduction to the English legal system. Wasn't too bad, but wasn't great.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: you have to buy a lot of things for your room if you stay at Leazes. like duvets and pillows, also kitchen things and a night lamp etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Flights were a bit more expensive than I thought. public transport is quite expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: anything you can imagine pretty much.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was in the book club but never attended any meetings. But they provide some cheap books which was nice. My friends were in some sports clubs, which seemed fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get around Britain. Take a trip to London, Edinburgh, York, Durham and Liverpool. Go to Quayside sunday market. Watch a match in St. James Park.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy because English people are nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I was mostly with other exchange students, but if you want to meet English people then go to the societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Geordie accent. 
The attendance :(

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Just friendliness in general. The pubs are fun.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring your own pillow, because English pillows are bad.
Try to make friends in your classes from the beginning - it makes classes much more fun.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My flatmates were a lot of fun and just hanging out with them was probably the best part of the exchange.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Actually motivating yourself to prepare for exams. But that's no different from in UCPH.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
